results_picks.reasoning: The consensus on Reds -1.5 shows a massive 220 edge_bps with the best price at +104 at FanDuel and -102 at MyBookie, compared to a median of -105 — the market is sharply mispriced on this line. Chase Burns is a legitimate frontline starter for Cincinnati while Kansas City counters with Luinder Avila, a significant mismatch in starter quality. The Twins moneyline carries a 275 edge_bps at -147 versus a median of -165, a substantial gap across 9 books. Joe Ryan is a solid, reliable starter for Minnesota while Chicago sends out David Sandlin, giving the Twins a clear pitching edge at home. At -147 on LowVig/BetOnline versus the market consensus around -165, there is genuine line value here.

The Over 8.0 sits at +103 best versus a median of even money, generating 73.9 edge_bps and positive expected value at a plus-money price. Griffin Jax is a reliever being used as a starter for Tampa Bay, suggesting a shorter leash and potential for a bullpen game that inflates run totals. Detroit's Ty Madden is also far from an ace, and with both teams running patchwork rotations this number has juice on the over side.

The Under 7.0 shows 208.6 edge_bps at -114 versus a median of -124, meaning FanDuel is significantly more generous than the rest of the market on the under side. Emerson Hancock is a legitimate strikeout arm for Seattle and Austin Warren is a low-leverage reliever masquerading as a starter for the Mets, which should limit run production early. A 7.0 total is already low but both pitching situations favor keeping this game under.

The Under 8.0 carries a 179.8 edge_bps at -107 versus a median of -115 across 9 books, representing nearly 2% of implied probability reclaimed. Jacob deGrom on the mound for Texas is a dominant ace when healthy and capable of suppressing any offense; paired against Michael McGreevy for St. Louis, the Rangers' starter gives this game a clear elite-versus-average pitching dynamic. At -107 versus -115 median, this is one of the sharpest total prices on the board today.

Arizona +1.5 shows 193.9 edge_bps at -111 versus a median of -120, a meaningful gap across all 9 books. Eduardo Rodriguez starting for Arizona is a serviceable left-hander against Emmet Sheehan for LA, and the Dodgers -1.5 run line at +106 best indicates oddsmakers see this as a close contest despite the h2h moneyline spread. Getting the D-backs to avoid a 2+ run loss at near-even money is strong value given the competitive pitching matchup.

Miami at +132 shows 174 edge_bps versus a median of +123, with BetOnline and LowVig both sitting 9 points above the market midpoint. Sandy Alcantara, when healthy, is a legitimate ace-level starter for the Marlins and represents a significant pitching upgrade over Washington's Cade Cavalli. At plus money with genuine line value and the superior starter on the mound, this is a worthwhile underdog play.

ig_carousel_topic.topic: Why your win rate matters less than your ROI
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
You can hit 55% and still lose money.
Here's why win rate alone lies to you.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors track wins and losses.
55% sounds great. But if your average winner pays -120 and your average loser costs -110, you're bleeding units every week.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
ROI tells the real story.
It measures net profit per dollar risked. A 52% bettor at +8% ROI beats a 57% bettor at -3% ROI every single time.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Real example:
Bettor A: 57 wins, 43 losses. Avg odds -130. Net: -1.8u
Bettor B: 52 wins, 48 losses. Avg odds +115. Net: +7.4u
Bettor B wins. By a lot.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Track your ROI. Not your record.
Our YTD: 274-230, +48.5u, 9.3% ROI across 55 days. Win rate is 54.4%. The edge lives in the odds, not the count.
